subject: Blended 18/24m renewal proposal with mid-term uplift option
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Blended 18/24m renewal proposal with mid-term uplift option

Hi Lina / Acme Procurement,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a short, structured proposal designed to: (1) sync our renewal window with your fiscal cadence, (2) give Acme headroom to scale mid-term, and (3) smooth spend across years. High level: a blended 18/24 month option where year 1 is a protected baseline with predictable unit pricing and year 2 includes a defined mid-term uplift clause tied to a usage/throughput trigger.

Key bullets:
- Term: 18 months effective 2028-10-01 with optional auto-extend to 24 months at pre-agreed uplift (details in attachment).
- Ramp schedule: measured quarterly uplift triggers (Q2/Q3) with a 30% cap on quarterly step-ups to avoid sudden invoice shocks.
- Co-terming: we can co-term subsidiary ACME Labs onto the same commitment at a pro-rated uplift.
- Billing: monthly invoicing with an option for 10% prepay discount if paid annually.
- Exit / true-up: standard true-up at renewal, but we propose a mid-term reconciliation window to adjust commit if usage deviates >25%.

Attachments: renewal_options_v1.pdf, midterm_uplift_clause_redline.docx, cost_model_assumptions.csv

Next steps: Can you confirm whether Acme prefers an 18m start (Oct 1) vs a straight 24m from Oct 1? If you want, I can turn this into a tracked DocuSign in the next 24–48 hours.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@acme.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.ai>, Aaron Wells <aaron.wells@acme.ai>, Acme AI Legal <legal@acme.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Blended 18/24m renewal proposal with mid-term uplift option

Jordan, thanks for the clear doc. A few clarifying items from our side before we route to legal and finance:
1) Auto-renew mechanics: what notice period do you require to opt out of the 24m auto-extend? 60/90 days?
2) Mid-term uplift trigger: can the trigger be based on 3-month rolling average rather than a single-quarter spike?
3) Pricing floor: we need assurance there's a floor so we don't pay more than X per token if model prices change.
4) Can you provide a pro-forma invoice for both 18m (no prepay) and 24m (annual prepay with 10% discount) so that finance can model cashflow?

Looping in Aaron (CFO) and legal. Please send redlines back to legal@acme.ai if possible.

Thanks,
Lina Ortiz
Head of Procurement, Acme AI
procurement@acme.ai | +1 415-555-2044

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 12:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Acme questions on triggers and auto-renew (proposal notes)

Team—quick notes before Jordan replies to Lina:
- Auto-renew notice: we typically require 60 days. We can make it 90 if legal asks, but revenue ops prefers 60.
- Trigger averaging: agree to a 3-month rolling average to smooth engineering spikes. We'll define the metric as "30-day rolling average tokens/sec" or usage dollars — whichever Acme prefers.
- Pricing floor: propose a CPI-linked floor: either fixed $/k token floor or tied to our published model tier price; finance to pick.
- Pro-forma: Marissa, can you prepare the 2-line pro-forma (18m monthly pay vs 24m annual prepay w/10%) with ARR and cashflow delta?

I'll draft a one-paragraph clause for the mid-term reconciliation and redline the docx.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Acme questions on triggers and auto-renew (proposal notes)

Karthik—sending the pro-forma (summary below). I'll attach the spreadsheet when we send externally.
- Option A (18m, monthly): baseline commit 1.2B tokens over 18m. Monthly billing at $0.0008/token. Estimated ARR impact: $640k annualized equivalence; cashflow: even.
- Option B (24m, annual prepay w/10%): commit 1.6B tokens; effective net $0.00072/token after discount. One upfront invoice for $1,152,000 (net of discount). ARR smoothing shows +12% in year 1 and +20% in year 2 versus Option A.
- Mid-term uplift mechanic: if 3mo rolling usage exceeds commit by >20% across any two consecutive quarters, a mid-term uplift tranche is billable at a pre-agreed uplift of +12% on token price for the excess. True-up at next invoice.

I'll attach cost_model_assumptions.csv and sample invoice lines.

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Revenue Strategist, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Acme AI Legal <legal@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Blended 18/24m renewal proposal with mid-term uplift option

Lina — thanks for the quick review and excellent questions. We've incorporated Acme feedback into the attached redline and a short pro-forma summary (see attachments). Summary of changes: 
- Auto-renew: notice window updated to 60 days.
- Uplift trigger: changed to a 3-month rolling average (definition included in clause).
- Pricing floor: we added a fixed floor of $0.00065/token or our published model tier price, whichever is higher; this protects both sides against extreme delta.
- Pro-forma: attached both scenarios (monthly billing vs annual prepay).

If that looks good, I'll generate a DocuSign package with the chosen term sheet and mid-term uplift addendum for signature. Here is a preview link: https://docusign.example/send/abc123 (expires in 7 days).

Requested ask: Lina, can you confirm whether Acme prefers Option A (18m monthly) or Option B (24m annual prepay) by EOD Wed, Aug 2 so we can lock pricing and reserve capacity? If you choose Option B we'll also queue Dedicated pool capacity for Oct 1 start.

Best,
Jordan
--

Jordan — appreciate the updates. This is helpful; procurement + finance are aligned to Option B (24m annual prepay) assuming the DocuSign reflects the pricing floor and the 3-month rolling trigger clause as redlined. We'll have legal confirm a couple of small wording points but expect to sign the package by Aug 6 to secure capacity. Please proceed with the DocuSign and share the final packet with legal@acme.ai.

Thanks,
Lina
